sources.entry: Yacy - Peer based, decentralized search engine server. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Java/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: YaCy is a self-hostable, peer-to-peer search engine server with a built-in web crawler, web interface, and an optional decentralized search network.
summary.what_it_does: YaCy bundles a search index server, a web front-end for searching and creating indexes, and a web crawler with a scheduler that keeps the index fresh. Search portals can be placed on an intranet, and a network scanner can discover HTTP, FTP and SMB servers. Each installation can exchange index data with other YaCy peers over a built-in peer-to-peer protocol, or it can be set to local-only operation so searches use only the local index. Its interfaces are HTTP/XML and HTTP/JSON, with shell scripts in the /bin subdirectory that call the web interface. The README says privacy was a primary motivation for the project.
use_cases: run a private personal search engine
crawl and index websites on a schedule
discover HTTP, FTP and SMB servers on a network
search without sending queries to a public index
embed search results in a custom web application
how_to_run: docker run -d --name yacy_search_server -p 8090:8090 -p 8443:8443 -v yacy_search_server_data:/opt/yacy_search_server/DATA --restart unless-stopped --log-opt max-size=200m --log-opt max-file=2 yacy/yacy_search_server:latest
notable: Peer-to-peer search network where instances share indexes, with an opt-out to local-only search
Built-in web crawler with a scheduler for keeping indexes fresh
Network scanner for discovering HTTP, FTP and SMB servers
Machine-readable XML and JSON interfaces behind the web UI, plus shell API scripts
caveats: The README recommends compiling from git sources; pre-compiled packages are not built regularly
Default admin account is admin/yacy and must be changed after installation
Windows installer requires building with NSIS and Ant
